DqCRgPi_jwo.speaker: adnan
DqCRgPi_jwo.speaker_note: single speaker teaching his weekly Tazkiyah series in his own voice
DqCRgPi_jwo.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: The Rituals, Episode 21
DqCRgPi_jwo.one_line: The sitting between prostrations as sincere repentance, the meaning of the tashahhud and salam, and salah as an act of love for Allah.
DqCRgPi_jwo.summary: This closing session on the movements of salah takes up the sitting between the two prostrations, which he frames as an apology to Allah. Real istighfar requires three things: sensitivity to sin, genuine conviction that the act is wrong, and an intention backed by a concrete plan not to repeat it. He uses his exercise of asking people to list fifty sins, contrasted with the Prophet seeking forgiveness a hundred times a day, to show that the count depends on how high a standard one holds oneself to. Focusing on one's own sins also removes arrogance toward others. Istighfar is the only healthy relationship with the past, as Surah An-Nasr pairs praise for success with seeking forgiveness. He then explains the tashahhud, addressing the Prophet as a present teacher, greeting all righteous servants as part of one ummah, the equality of the rows, turning to people with the salam, and closing with salawat. He argues that salah fails without its foundations: guidance, gratitude free of vanity, understanding dua and healthy remorse. Allah needs none of our worship, so the only thing we offer is love, which is why salah gives every other good deed its meaning. He asks listeners to review the series and pray one slow voluntary prayer applying every tip.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah as a skill set, and why these salah tips
outline.gist: Tazkiyah teaches principles and the skill of handling one's own unique obstacles; the salah tips are a practical way to start improving prayer while the deeper work takes time.

outline.heading: The sitting between prostrations is an apology
outline.gist: Sujud is for requesting, the sitting is for seeking forgiveness with humility and remorse; focusing on one's own sins leaves no room to judge others on assumptions.

outline.heading: Self-criticism puts you on a path of improvement
outline.gist: Anyone who can identify a mistake, feel remorse and intend not to repeat it will improve over time; failing to think of a single sin is itself the first problem to fix.

outline.heading: The fifty sins exercise and the Prophet's hundred istighfar
outline.gist: People struggle to list fifty sins while the Prophet repented a hundred times a day; the difference is sensitivity to Allah's commands and the standard one holds oneself to.

outline.heading: You must be convinced a sin is a sin
outline.gist: Remorse is impossible for an act you do not truly believe is wrong; like a hollow apology, it changes nothing, and that unexamined sin is the one you will be questioned about along with the excuses we invent.

outline.heading: Salah contains every core aspect of being Muslim
outline.gist: Guidance, exaltation, gratitude, requesting and remorse all live in the prayer; Islam asks remorse only for what you yourself did, not for something inherited.

outline.heading: Repentance needs an intention and a plan
outline.gist: An apology with no intention to stop is empty; while seeking forgiveness, work out which habit, company or circumstance leads to the sin and adjust something each time.

outline.heading: Istighfar as a self-regulating system of growth
outline.gist: Seeking forgiveness at least seventeen times a day lets Muslims correct themselves without needing others to point out faults; being sinful is normal, refusing to acknowledge it is the problem.

outline.heading: The only healthy relationship with the past
outline.gist: The sitting addresses the past while sujud addresses present and future; Surah An-Nasr pairs praising Allah for victory with asking forgiveness for what could have been done better.

outline.heading: Each movement covers a part of life's struggle
outline.gist: Praise covers successes, istighfar covers regrets, dua in sujud covers hopes and fears, standing covers confusion, and tasbih covers what you cannot control.

outline.heading: The tashahhud: greeting Allah
outline.gist: One cannot give salam to Allah who is As-Salam, so the tahiyyat declares that all signs of life and all worship belong to Him, and the Prophet is then addressed directly.

outline.heading: The Prophet as a present teacher and chaperone
outline.gist: Greeting the Prophet in the second person reflects that he taught this prayer and is present as the role model whose example frames every good deed, without being worshipped.

outline.heading: Praying as part of an ummah
outline.gist: Greeting all righteous servants shows that even a lone prayer is offered in the plural, as part of the nation of Muhammad turning to Allah together.

outline.heading: Equality in the rows and running the prayer well
outline.gist: The rows are the one gathering with no VIP seats; those behind the imam exist to run the ritual, and each generation must be trained so the prayer keeps its meaning.

outline.heading: Ending with salam to the people around you
outline.gist: The Prophet is watching like a teacher grading an exam; the closing salam is said looking at the people beside you, and closing the eyes to focus is permissible though not recommended.

outline.heading: Closing with salawat on the Prophet and Ibrahim
outline.gist: Just as good gatherings end with salawat, the prayer ends by connecting it to the chosen lineage through whom guidance came.

outline.heading: Practise all the tips in one slow voluntary prayer
outline.gist: Set aside a sunnah prayer, perhaps at night, to go through every movement deliberately instead of praying on cruise control.

outline.heading: Voluntary prayers and taraweeh are the training ground
outline.gist: Sunnah prayers allow flexibility to practise, yet people rush taraweeh, so many live and die without one meaningful prayer; an early scholar hoped for even one or two prayers accepted.

outline.heading: Be concerned if salah gives you nothing
outline.gist: If prayer brings no growth, closeness or peace, that must be pursued personally, and it requires understanding guidance and why the Quran matters.

outline.heading: The nafs resists praise and gratitude
outline.gist: The ego rejects that Allah is flawless and we are flawed; true hamd requires removing vanity and disgruntlement about what one did or did not get.

outline.heading: Understanding dua: no entitlement and clear articulation
outline.gist: We are owed nothing and already in debt to Allah; good dua defines exactly what is wanted and why, and articulating a problem is a large part of solving it, including knowing what is reasonable to ask.

outline.heading: Healthy remorse and the core concepts behind salah
outline.gist: Remorse must not become debilitating or erase self-value; salah is built on these core concepts and forces the question of purpose.

outline.heading: Interlude
Salah as a portal facing the first house
outline.gist: Facing the Kaaba, built from the beginning and the focus of all prophets, reorients the believer physically in a way that mirrors a spiritual direction.

outline.heading: Allah needs none of our worship
outline.gist: Worship asked by someone who needs it would be selfish; Allah gains nothing, and humans alone have the option to refuse, so voluntary worship from a selfish creature is pure love.

outline.heading: Every command benefits us; only love goes to Him
outline.gist: Contemplating His word, gratitude, appropriate speech and remorse all build our character, while the only thing projected toward Allah is the love behind them.

outline.heading: Reward and punishment for the nafs, love for the spirit
outline.gist: Carrot and stick motivate the animal self, while the higher self is moved by returning love; only lovers rise at night to meet the one they love.

outline.heading: Without salah other good deeds lose their meaning

outline.heading: There is always something to do in each movement
outline.gist: Review the sessions and use them as a map: contemplate verses while standing, keep magnifying, keep up dua, think of a sin while sitting, and count blessings; salah is a form of therapy.

31:20.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَوۡاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَأَسۡبَغَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ نِعَمَهُۥ ظَٰهِرَةࣰ وَبَاطِنَةࣰۗ وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَٰدِلُ فِي ٱللَّهِ بِغَيۡرِ عِلۡمࣲ وَلَا هُدࣰ ى وَلَا كِتَٰبࣲ مُّنِيرࣲ‏
31:20.en: Do you not see that Allah has made subject to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and amply bestowed upon you His favors, [both] apparent and unapparent? But of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book [from Him]

31:21.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَا وَجَدۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ يَدۡعُوهُمۡ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
31:21.en: And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our fathers." Even if Satan was inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze

31:22.ar: ۞وَمَن يُسۡلِمۡ وَجۡهَهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحۡسِنࣱ فَقَدِ ٱسۡتَمۡسَكَ بِٱلۡعُرۡوَةِ ٱلۡوُثۡقَىٰۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡأُمُورِ
31:22.en: And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good - then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold. And to Allah will be the outcome of [all] matters

31:23.ar: وَمَن كَفَرَ فَلَا يَحۡزُنكَ كُفۡرُهُۥٓۚ إِلَيۡنَا مَرۡجِعُهُمۡ فَنُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
31:23.en: And whoever has disbelieved - let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts

31:24.ar: نُمَتِّعُهُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا ثُمَّ نَضۡطَرُّهُمۡ إِلَىٰ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظࣲ‏
31:24.en: We grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a massive punishment

45:13.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا مِّنۡهُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
45:13.en: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought

14:33.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ دَآئِبَيۡنِۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ
14:33.en: And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, continuous [in orbit], and subjected for you the night and the day

14:34.ar: وَءَاتَىٰكُم مِّن كُلِّ مَا سَأَلۡتُمُوهُۚ وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحۡصُوهَآۗ إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ لَظَلُومࣱ كَفَّارࣱ‏
14:34.en: And He gave you from all you asked of Him. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is [generally] most unjust and ungrateful

31:12.ar: وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَا لُقۡمَٰنَ ٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ أَنِ ٱشۡكُرۡ لِلَّهِۚ وَمَن يَشۡكُرۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدࣱ‏
31:12.en: And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom [and said], "Be grateful to Allah." And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever denies [His favor] - then indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy

2:8.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤۡمِنِينَ
2:8.en: And of the people are some who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers

22:11.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعۡبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرۡفࣲۖ فَإِنۡ أَصَابَهُۥ خَيۡرٌ ٱطۡمَأَنَّ بِهِۦۖ وَإِنۡ أَصَابَتۡهُ فِتۡنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦ خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡخُسۡرَانُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
22:11.en: And of the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If he is touched by good, he is reassured by it; but if he is struck by trial, he turns on his face [to the other direction]. He has lost [this] world and the Hereafter. That is what is the manifest loss

2:170.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَآ أَلۡفَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَهۡتَدُونَ
2:170.en: And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that which we found our fathers doing." Even though their fathers understood nothing, nor were they guided

5:104.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ وَإِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ قَالُواْ حَسۡبُنَا مَا وَجَدۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَهۡتَدُونَ
5:104.en: And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing, nor were they guided

103:3.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ
103:3.en: Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience

4:46.ar: مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ غَيۡرَ مُسۡمَعࣲ وَرَٰعِنَا لَيَّۢا بِأَلۡسِنَتِهِمۡ وَطَعۡنࣰ ا فِي ٱلدِّينِۚ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَأَطَعۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ وَٱنظُرۡنَا لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَقۡوَمَ وَلَٰكِن لَّعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُفۡرِهِمۡ فَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
4:46.en: Among the Jews are those who distort words from their [proper] usages and say, "We hear and disobey" and "Hear but be not heard" and "Ra'ina," twisting their tongues and defaming the religion. And if they had said [instead], "We hear and obey" and "Wait for us [to understand]," it would have been better for them and more suitable. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, except for a few

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error

31:15.ar: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشۡرِكَ بِي مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَاۖ وَصَاحِبۡهُمَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَعۡرُوفࣰ اۖ وَٱتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ مَنۡ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّۚ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
31:15.en: But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do

31:2.en: These are verses of the wise Book

31:3.en: As guidance and mercy for the doers of good

4EG55pE7Ey4.speaker_note: Continues his own Sunday Arabic tafsir of Surat Luqman, referring to his previous weeks' lessons
4EG55pE7Ey4.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Luqman (Verses 20-24)
4EG55pE7Ey4.one_line: The commentary after Luqman's counsel: a creation made subservient to us, gratitude between generations, and why following forefathers blindly is rejected.
4EG55pE7Ey4.summary: After explaining how surahs are built, he reads verses 20 to 24 as Allah's commentary on Luqman's counsel. The plural address shows that the relationship between generations, like any relationship, works only when both sides make an effort. Everything in the heavens and earth has been made subservient to humans, which makes them responsible for its care and use, and blessings cover people outwardly and inwardly. Gratitude is the lens through which elders and children should see one another: as blessings rather than burdens; he explains his own patience with youth by not knowing which of them Allah will use for great things. Placed right after a wise father's counsel, the verse condemning those who follow their forefathers shows that the young must neither worship nor dismiss the previous generation. Submission belongs to Allah alone; even scholars and companions erred, and Islam survived by balancing inherited and new. Parenting methods from the home countries are a means to righteousness and success, not a sacred end. Whoever submits to Allah while doing excellent work, setting aside pride, holds the firmest handhold. As for those who will not listen, their reckoning is with Allah; the believer's job is to speak, call and model.

outline.heading: Recap: the surah builds the bond between generations
outline.gist: The first nineteen verses centre on Luqman's counsel; the surah's aim is the relationship between parents and children.

outline.heading: How surahs are structured
outline.gist: Some have introduction, body and conclusion; some are sections; some build to a pivotal verse followed by commentary.

outline.heading: Short surahs as single pills of medicine
outline.gist: The last juz' presents one idea quickly; Luqman, though short, has an introduction, pivotal verses and commentary.

outline.heading: Recitation of the commentary verses
outline.gist: Recitation of the verses on subjugated creation, those who dispute about Allah, and following forefathers.

outline.heading: Do you not all see: both sides must try
outline.gist: The plural address speaks to both parent and child; any marriage, friendship or work relationship fails if one side makes no effort.

outline.heading: Subjugation: creation exists for you
outline.gist: Taskhir differs from creation: the planet was made with you as its purpose.

outline.heading: What is subjugated to you is your responsibility
outline.gist: You must protect, care for and use well what serves you, as far as you are able.

outline.heading: Isbagh: a complete covering
outline.gist: The word as in completing wudu in hardship; doing a hard command fully brings great reward.

outline.heading: Blessings outward and inward lead to gratitude
outline.gist: A planet with everything needed, plus guidance and intellect; the verse returns to Luqman's first lesson of gratitude.

outline.heading: Gratitude for each other across generations
outline.gist: Elderly parents seen as a burden and children blamed for lost freedom ruin relationships; their mere presence is a blessing despite the hardship.

outline.heading: A grateful mind sees elders and youth differently
outline.gist: The verse is comprehensive in gratitude; you can see the same person through twenty eyes and must choose gratitude.

outline.heading: Why he is patient with young people
outline.gist: He never knows which child may become a Salahuddin, so he sees potential where others see noise and bad manners.

outline.heading: Those who dispute about Allah without knowledge
outline.gist: The Quran uses 'among people' to expose ignorant acts without naming people; they argue about the One who gave them everything.

outline.heading: Be unlike the ungrateful
outline.gist: If people speak ill even of Allah, expect criticism yourself; they lack knowledge, guidance and an illuminating book, so be grateful instead.

outline.heading: Following forefathers right after a wise father
outline.gist: Why the verse on blind ancestral following comes directly after Luqman's counsel.

outline.heading: The Quran does not ask for blind acceptance
outline.gist: The Quran's quarrel is with blind following; the placement is deliberate, warning against misreading Luqman's story.

outline.heading: Neither sanctify nor dismiss the elders
outline.gist: No one is all right or all wrong; only the eye of gratitude lets you separate what benefits from what harms.

outline.heading: Quraysh and their fathers
outline.gist: The Prophet spent twenty years arguing that respected fathers can still be wrong; some replied they would follow them to hell.

outline.heading: Knowledge cannot grow inside our predecessors' cloaks
outline.gist: Elders cannot decide every detail of their children's lives; humanity would not advance otherwise.

outline.heading: The religion of your father Ibrahim
outline.gist: If it is about ancestors, go back to Ibrahim and Adam; yet his call was to Allah, not to ancestry.

outline.heading: Balance: you need someone who walked the road
outline.gist: Neither take all nor reject all; whoever has no elder should find one who has walked the path before you.

outline.heading: Mutual counsel is two-way
outline.gist: Al-Asr: counsel among believers is mutual; even Allah responds to His servants' prayers and questions.

outline.heading: We hear and disobey versus we hear and obey
outline.gist: Those who twisted words with their prophets, against the right way: hear and obey, then ask for time.

outline.heading: Submit to no one but Allah
outline.gist: No believer has a choice once Allah and His Messenger decide; complete submission belongs to Allah alone.

outline.heading: Verify that it is really the Prophet's meaning
outline.gist: Check that a preacher quoting the Prophet conveys his actual intent and is not bending it for an agenda.

outline.heading: Scholars and companions were not infallible
outline.gist: Discovering that a great figure erred should not shake faith; they were human and watched constantly.

outline.heading: Islam survived by balancing old and new
outline.gist: What is new today is old in twenty years; Quraysh rejected the Prophet's message as new.

outline.heading: Recitation: whoever submits his face to Allah
outline.gist: Recitation of the verses on submission, the firm handhold and those who disbelieve.

outline.heading: Islam means surrendering your own will
outline.gist: Submitting yourself as one surrenders to police: replacing your choice with Allah's.

outline.heading: Do not surrender yourself to your parents
outline.gist: Parents may command what contradicts Allah or causes harm; he received objections after saying Luqman did not demand birr.

outline.heading: Parenting methods from the home countries
outline.gist: Methods used where we grew up may not all work in this country; what matters is the purpose.

outline.heading: Upbringing is a means, not the goal
outline.gist: The goal is a righteous, successful child; keep the methods that worked on you and drop those that did not or no longer will.

outline.heading: Submitting the face: setting pride aside
outline.gist: The face stands for the self; elders' and youths' pride toward each other blocks the relationship.

outline.heading: While doing excellent work
outline.gist: Echoing the surah's opening on the muhsinin: the aim is achieving the good, not showing off or being proven right.

outline.heading: The firmest handhold
outline.gist: Al-'urwah al-wuthqa holds under any weight, unlike attractive human ideas that collapse under criticism.

outline.heading: Do not grieve over those who disbelieve
outline.gist: Some, old or young, will never listen; Allah will inform them of their error on the Day they return.

outline.heading: He knows what is in the breasts; brief enjoyment
outline.gist: Allah exposes even intentions; a lifetime of power is little before being compelled to a harsh punishment.

outline.heading: Your task is to call, not to judge
outline.gist: Do not take on Allah's role of punishing or reckoning; talk, invite and be an example.
